title: The night Berlin's church burned

facts.text: On the night of 22 to 23 November 1943 RAF Bomber Command sent 764 aircraft against Berlin: 469 Lancasters, 234 Halifaxes, 50 Stirlings and 11 Mosquitos. It was the largest force yet sent to the city.

The raid was part of the Battle of Berlin, the bomber campaign Air Marshal Arthur Harris had opened on 18 November. He predicted: "It will cost us between 400 and 500 aircraft. It will cost Germany the war."
Berlin lay under cloud, but pathfinders marked the target by radar, so the cloud no longer protected the city.
Dry weather let the fires spread into several firestorms. The worst damage fell on the residential districts west of the centre: Tiergarten, Charlottenburg, Schoeneberg and Spandau.
About 2,000 Berliners were killed that night and 175,000 lost their homes. The RAF lost 26 aircraft.
The next night 383 more bombers came back. About 1,000 more people were killed and another 100,000 were made homeless.

Among the buildings hit was the Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church, built in the 1890s in memory of Emperor Wilhelm I. It was badly damaged; the broken stump of the main spire and much of the entrance hall survived.
Charlottenburg Palace, the Berlin Zoo and the British, French, Italian and Japanese embassies were damaged or destroyed in the same raid.

After the war the church's trustees chose to rebuild, but how was argued over until the late 1950s. The architect Egon Eiermann, who won the 1956 design competition, first planned to tear the ruined spire down.
Berliners protested, calling the ruin the heart of Berlin, and Eiermann changed his design to keep it. His new church went up beside the old tower between 1959 and 1963.
Inside the ruined tower's hall today is a cross made from nails out of the roof timbers of Coventry Cathedral, which German bombers destroyed on 14 November 1940.

body:
Berliners fought to save a ruin. In the 1950s an architect planned to tear down the broken spire of their memorial church, and they would not let him.

22 to 23 November 1943. Overnight, 764 RAF bombers came over Berlin, the largest force yet sent to the city. In dry weather the fires grew into firestorms in the western districts. About 2,000 people were killed and 175,000 lost their homes. The Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church burned, leaving the stump of its main spire.

Berliners called the ruin the heart of their city. Egon Eiermann changed his design, and his new church rose beside the old tower. Inside the tower hangs a cross made from nails of Coventry Cathedral, destroyed by German bombers in 1940.
threads:
Berliners fought to save a ruin, and won.

22 to 23 November 1943. 764 RAF bombers hit Berlin, about 2,000 people died, and the Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church burned down to the stump of its spire. When an architect later planned to clear it away, Berliners protested. The ruin still stands, with a cross of Coventry Cathedral nails inside.
